### 1.1-1.5 Problem Analysis

**Problem Summary:** 
The `pixel_array` property in pydicom returns incorrect pixel data values for JPEG2000Lossless compressed DICOM files. The pixel values are not respecting the proper bit depth (`BitsStored`) leading to incorrect scaling.

**Technical Details:**
- **Method affected**: `pixel_array` property
- **Transfer Syntax**: JPEG2000Lossless 
- **Key attributes**: `BitsStored`, `RescaleSlope`, `RescaleIntercept`
- **Error manifestation**: Incorrect pixel value ranges (256 instead of 4096 for 12-bit, 65536 instead of 4096)

**Clear Problem Statement:**
When reading JPEG2000Lossless compressed DICOM files, pydicom's `pixel_array` property incorrectly interprets the pixel data, not properly accounting for the `BitsStored` attribute. This results in pixel values that are scaled incorrectly compared to what other DICOM viewers produce.

**Reproduction Steps:**
1. Load a JPEG2000Lossless DICOM file using `pydicom.read_file()`
2. Access the `pixel_array` property
3. Apply `RescaleSlope` and `RescaleIntercept` transformations
4. Observe incorrect pixel value ranges

**Best Practices for Testing/Fixing:**
- Understand JPEG2000 decoding pipeline in pydicom
- Verify BitsStored handling during decompression
- Test with various bit depths (12-bit, 16-bit examples mentioned)
- Ensure backward compatibility with existing functionality

     9	# *pydicom*
    10	
    11	*pydicom* is a pure Python package for working with [DICOM](https://www.dicomstandard.org/) files.
    12	It lets you read, modify and write DICOM data in an easy "pythonic" way. As a pure Python package,
    13	*pydicom* can run anywhere Python runs without any other requirements, although if you're working
    14	with *Pixel Data* then we recommend you also install [NumPy](https://numpy.org).
    15	
    16	Note that *pydicom* is a general-purpose DICOM framework concerned with
    17	reading and writing DICOM datasets. In order to keep the
    18	project manageable, it does not handle the specifics of individual SOP classes
    19	or other aspects of DICOM. Other libraries both inside and outside the
    20	[pydicom organization](https://github.com/pydicom) are based on *pydicom*
    21	and provide support for other aspects of DICOM, and for more
    22	specific applications.
    23	
    24	Examples are [pynetdicom](https://github.com/pydicom/pynetdicom), which
    25	is a Python library for DICOM networking, and [deid](https://github.com/pydicom/deid),
    26	which supports the anonymization of DICOM files.
    27	
    28	
    29	## Installation
    30	
    31	Using [pip](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/):
    32	```
    33	pip install pydicom
    34	```
    35	Using [conda](https://docs.conda.io/en/latest/):
    36	```
    37	conda install -c conda-forge pydicom
    38	```
    39	
    40	For more information, including installation instructions for the development version, see the [installation guide](https://pydicom.github.io/pydicom/stable/tutorials/installation.html).

    47	## *Pixel Data*
    48	
    49	Compressed and uncompressed *Pixel Data* is always available to
    50	be read, changed and written as [bytes](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes-objects):
    51	```python
    52	>>> from pydicom import dcmread
    53	>>> from pydicom.data import get_testdata_file
    54	>>> path = get_testdata_file("CT_small.dcm")
    55	>>> ds = dcmread(path)
    56	>>> type(ds.PixelData)
    57	<class 'bytes'>
    58	>>> len(ds.PixelData)
    59	32768
    60	>>> ds.PixelData[:2]
    61	b'\xaf\x00'
    62	
    63	```
    64	
    65	If [NumPy](https://www.numpy.org) is installed, *Pixel Data* can be converted to an [ndarray](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.html) using the [Dataset.pixel_array](https://pydicom.github.io/pydicom/stable/reference/generated/pydicom.dataset.Dataset.html#pydicom.dataset.Dataset.pixel_array) property:
    66	
    67	```python
    68	>>> arr = ds.pixel_array
    69	>>> arr.shape
    70	(128, 128)
    71	>>> arr
    72	array([[175, 180, 166, ..., 203, 207, 216],
    73	       [186, 183, 157, ..., 181, 190, 239],
    74	       [184, 180, 171, ..., 152, 164, 235],
    75	       ...,
    76	       [906, 910, 923, ..., 922, 929, 927],
    77	       [914, 954, 938, ..., 942, 925, 905],
    78	       [959, 955, 916, ..., 911, 904, 909]], dtype=int16)
    79	```
    80	### Decompressing *Pixel Data*
    81	#### JPEG, JPEG-LS and JPEG 2000
    82	Converting JPEG, JPEG-LS or JPEG 2000 compressed *Pixel Data* to an ``ndarray`` requires installing one or more additional Python libraries. For information on which libraries are required, see the [pixel data handler documentation](https://pydicom.github.io/pydicom/stable/guides/user/image_data_handlers.html#guide-compressed).
    83	
    84	#### RLE
    85	Decompressing RLE *Pixel Data* only requires NumPy, however it can be quite slow. You may want to consider [installing one or more additional Python libraries](https://pydicom.github.io/pydicom/stable/guides/user/image_data_compression.html) to speed up the process.
    86	
    87	### Compressing *Pixel Data*
    88	Information on compressing *Pixel Data* using one of the below formats can be found in the corresponding [encoding guides](https://pydicom.github.io/pydicom/stable/guides/encoding/index.html). These guides cover the specific requirements for each encoding method and we recommend you be familiar with them when performing image compression.
    89	
    90	#### JPEG-LS, JPEG 2000
    91	Compressing image data from an ``ndarray`` or ``bytes`` object to JPEG-LS or JPEG 2000 requires installing the following:
    92	
    93	* JPEG-LS requires [pyjpegls](https://github.com/pydicom/pyjpegls)
    94	* JPEG 2000 requires [pylibjpeg](https://github.com/pydicom/pylibjpeg) and the [pylibjpeg-openjpeg](https://github.com/pydicom/pylibjpeg-openjpeg) plugin
    95	
    96	#### RLE
    97	Compressing using RLE requires no additional packages but can be quite slow. It can be sped up by installing [pylibjpeg](https://github.com/pydicom/pylibjpeg) with the [pylibjpeg-rle](https://github.com/pydicom/pylibjpeg-rle) plugin, or [gdcm](https://github.com/tfmoraes/python-gdcm).
    98

   100	## Examples
   101	More [examples](https://pydicom.github.io/pydicom/stable/auto_examples/index.html) are available in the documentation.
   102	
   103	**Change a patient's ID**
   104	```python
   105	from pydicom import dcmread
   106	
   107	ds = dcmread("/path/to/file.dcm")
   108	# Edit the (0010,0020) 'Patient ID' element
   109	ds.PatientID = "12345678"
   110	ds.save_as("/path/to/file_updated.dcm")
   111	```
   112	
   113	**Display the Pixel Data**
   114	
   115	With [NumPy](https://numpy.org) and [matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org/)
   116	```python
   117	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
   118	from pydicom import dcmread
   119	from pydicom.data import get_testdata_file
   120	
   121	# The path to a pydicom test dataset
   122	path = get_testdata_file("CT_small.dcm")
   123	ds = dcmread(path)
   124	# `arr` is a numpy.ndarray
   125	arr = ds.pixel_array
   126	
   127	plt.imshow(arr, cmap="gray")
   128	plt.show()
   129	```
